deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §71 of the unpublished continuation of Ramanujan's 'Highly composite numbers' (1915). Here Σ_{-s}(N) is the maximum of σ_{-s}(n) = Σ_{d|n} d^{-s} over n ≤ N, attained at generalised superior highly composite numbers. The estimates assume the Riemann hypothesis. S_s(x) is the oscillating sum over the nontrivial zeros ρ. On the previous page, (377) gave log Σ_{-s}(N) as a sum of logarithmic-integral terms Li((log N)^{1-ks}), plus a correction coming from x_2 ≈ 2^{1/(2s)}√(log N) (378). Case I (0<s<1/2) gave (379).

Case II, s = 1/2 (eq. 380). Let s → 1/2 in (377), using (358) and (378) as the previous page indicates. The singular pieces −½Li((log N)^{1−2s}), −½Li((log N)^{1/2−s}) and Li(x_2^{1−2s}) combine with log|ζ(s)|. The result is
Σ_{-1/2}(N) = −√2 ζ(1/2) · exp{ Li(√log N) + (2 log 2 − 1 + S_{1/2}(log N))/log log N + O(1/(log log N)^2) }.
The prefactor is positive because ζ(1/2) ≈ −1.4604 < 0. I have not re-derived the constant 2 log 2 − 1; the limiting computation is not on this page.

Case III, s > 1/2 (eq. 381). Now n = [1 + 1/(2s)] = 1, and the terms Li((log N)^{1−ks}) for k ≥ 2 are absorbed into the constant. The x_2-terms combine with coefficient −2s(2^{1/(2s)} − 1)/(1 − 2s) = +2s(2^{1/(2s)} − 1)/(2s − 1), the same expression as in (379). This gives
Σ_{-s}(N) = |ζ(s)| exp{ Li((log N)^{1−s}) + [2s(2^{1/(2s)} − 1)/(2s − 1)] (log N)^{1/2−s}/log log N + S_s(log N)/log log N + O((log N)^{1/2−s}/(log log N)^2) }.

The case s → 1 (eq. 382). Write L = log log N and u = (1 − s)L.
- [my filling] Use Li(e^u) = γ + log|u| + u + O(u^2) and ζ(s) = 1/(s − 1) + γ + O(s − 1).
- Then ζ(s) e^{Li((log N)^{1−s})} → e^γ log log N.
- The coefficient becomes 2(√2 − 1), times (log N)^{−1/2}/log log N.
- Expand e^ε ≈ 1 + ε and multiply by e^γ log log N.
Result: Σ_{-1}(N) = e^γ{ log log N + 2(√2 − 1)/√(log N) + S_1(log N) + O(1/(√(log N) log log N)) }.

Limit bounds. [my filling] Under RH, S_1(x) is a sum of terms x^{ρ−1}/(ρ(ρ−1)), so √x |S_1(x)| ≤ Σ_ρ 1/|ρ|^2 = Σ_ρ 1/(ρ(1 − ρ)) = 2 + γ − log 4π ≈ 0.0461. Hence
- limsup (Σ_{-1}(N) − e^γ log log N)√(log N) ≤ e^γ(2(√2 − 1) + 2 + γ − log 4π) = e^γ(2√2 + γ − log 4π) ≈ 1.558;
- liminf of the same quantity ≥ e^γ(2√2 − 4 − γ + log 4π) ≈ 1.393.
Both numerical values are correct.

Remarks on σ_s and s → ∞.
- The maximum order of σ_s(N) is N^s Σ_{-s}(N), since σ_s(n) = n^s σ_{-s}(n).
- As s → ∞ the exponent thresholds x_r → x_1^{1/r}. So the generalised superior highly composite number tends to exp(θ(x) + θ(x^{1/2}) + θ(x^{1/3}) + …) = e^{ψ(x)} = lcm(1, …, [x]).

Without the prime number theorem. Using only Chebyshev-type bounds θ(x) ≍ x, one has x_1 ≍ log N. The results therefore hold with log N replaced by (log N)e^{O(1)}; this is the marginal insertion 'log'. In particular (383): Σ_{-1}(N) = e^γ{log log N + O(1)}, i.e. σ(n)/n ≤ e^γ log log n + O(1).
errors: No substantive errors detected. The numerical constants 1.558 and 1.393 check out.
The limsup/liminf bounds rely implicitly on RH. The assumption is what makes |S_1(x)|√x ≤ Σ1/|ρ|^2 = 2+γ−log4π hold; this is implicit and not stated on the page.
The final sentence, as written in the main text, says 'changing N to N e^{O(1)}'. The marginal insertion makes it 'log N to (log N) e^{O(1)}'. Only the corrected version yields (383).
The constant 2 log 2 − 1 in (380) comes from a delicate limit s→1/2 that is not shown on this page. It is not independently verified here.

results.what: Asymptotic for max_{n≤N} σ_{-1/2}(n) under RH, with constant −√2ζ(1/2) and secondary term (2log2−1+S_{1/2})/loglogN
results.modern_name: Maximal order of σ_{-s}(n) via generalised superior highly composite numbers (Ramanujan's lost HCN paper)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan; published posthumously by Nicolas & Robin (Ramanujan J. 1, 1997)

results.modern_name: Maximal order of σ_{-s}(n) under RH

results.what: Under RH, σ(n)/n ≤ e^γ(loglog n + 2(√2−1)/√log n + S_1(log n) + ...), with limsup/liminf of (Σ_{-1}(N)−e^γ loglogN)√logN between 1.393 and 1.558
results.modern_name: Ramanujan's RH-conditional bound for σ(n)/n, precursor of Robin's criterion (1984)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (1915 manuscript, published 1997); Robin 1984 for the RH equivalence σ(n)<e^γ n loglog n

results.what: As s→∞, generalised superior HC numbers tend to lcm(1..x)=e^{ψ(x)}
results.modern_name: Limit of generalised superior highly composite numbers; e^{ψ(x)}=lcm

results.what: Without PNT: σ(n)/n ≤ e^γ loglog n + O(1)

deep.surprise_reason: This page belongs to the well-known suppressed part of Ramanujan's highly composite numbers paper. It was published and annotated by Nicolas and Robin in 1997, and its RH-conditional σ(n)/n bounds are widely cited as Ramanujan's precursor to Robin's criterion.
